children: By Staff Writer
Dubai-based Grovy Developers is not currently seeing any major or unusual cost escalation for its branded-residential project on Dubai Islands despite the ongoing Middle East conflict.
“Procurement has already commenced and working with larger suppliers has provided greater stability,” CEO Abhishek Jalan told Zawya Projects.
He believes material costs may soften as logistics conditions gradually normalise.
Ramada Residences by Wyndham houses 68 housing units and is scheduled for handover in the third quarter of 2027.
The year is likely to see another launch, with two more planned for 2027.
“Our focus is on disciplined growth rather than simply announcing headline pipeline numbers,” he said.
Interview excerpts:
What are the biggest challenges that you expect during the construction of Ramada Residences by Wyndham at Dubai Islands?

As with any construction project, there are execution and planning risks that need to be closely managed. At present, the two key areas we are monitoring are material availability and timely delivery, as well as potential cost escalation.

The broader geopolitical and logistics environment can impact supply chains and transportation, so effective procurement planning is particularly important. For Ramada Residences, we are actively monitoring supplier availability and securing key materials in advance to minimise potential disruption and maintain construction progress.
Did the regional conflict lead to an increase in your construction costs compared to your initial planning?

The impact of geopolitical disruption on construction costs varies significantly by project stage. Generally, projects between approximately 25% and 75% complete face greater exposure to cost escalation, potentially upwards of 3%, while projects at earlier or more advanced stages may have lower exposure.

For Ramada Residences specifically, we are currently not seeing any major or unusual cost escalation. Procurement has already commenced, and working with larger suppliers has provided greater stability. With logistics conditions gradually normalising, there is potential for some softening in material costs going forward. We expect around 70–75 percent of key items to be finalised within the current and following quarter, giving us greater visibility on final procurement costs.
How do you monitor construction quality on your project?

Quality is monitored at every stage of construction through defined inspection checklists for each activity, rather than being assessed only at project completion. This allows any issues to be identified and addressed as the work progresses.

We are also continuously improving our processes through construction management software, which enables us to systematically track inspections, construction progress and quality controls throughout the project.
When do you expect to complete construction and start handing over units?

The project is currently on track, and we are not anticipating any delays at this stage. Our focus remains on maintaining construction progress and ensuring that handover takes place according to the planned timeline. We have close visibility of activities across the project and can fast-track certain works where required, giving us the flexibility to respond proactively to potential challenges.
How important is it for you to hand over the project on time?

Timely handover is extremely important to both the developer and the customer. At Ramada Residences, the construction-linked payment structure provides greater transparency, with customer payments aligned to actual construction progress.

This means investors deploy capital in line with on-site progress, while also having greater visibility into how their investment is being deployed. If there is any change to the construction timeline, payment deployment is correspondingly aligned with actual progress, providing customers with greater clarity throughout the development cycle.
How are you funding your project? Have you taken any bank loans, or is it self-funded through off-plan receipts?

We do not publicly disclose the specific funding structure of individual projects. We focus on maintaining a disciplined development approach and ensuring each project is adequately supported throughout its construction lifecycle.
How much land bank do you own in the UAE? Are you continuing to increase it?

Our strategy is increasingly focused on joint venture developments and partnerships with landowners rather than actively acquiring land outright. We see strong opportunities to work with landowners who bring strategic locations and assets, while we contribute our development expertise.

This approach allows us to utilise capital more efficiently and continue expanding our development pipeline in a disciplined manner. We remain open to further partnerships with landowners where there is a strong strategic fit.
How many projects do you plan to launch in 2026 and 2027? Can you share the value of your proposed investments?
We are currently planning one additional launch in 2026 and two projects in 2027. Our focus is on disciplined growth rather than simply announcing headline pipeline numbers.

The final investment value of each project will depend on factors including its location, product positioning and development structure, so we would prefer to provide those figures once the respective projects are finalised.
Are there plans to enter other emirates, particularly Ras Al Khaimah, and the Middle East?

At this stage, our strategy is to deepen our presence in Dubai rather than expand geographically for expansion’s sake. We believe Dubai offers strong long-term fundamentals, including a deep and diversified property market, strong international investor demand, liquidity and a broad economic base.

For us, it is important to focus on markets where multiple economic and demographic fundamentals support demand. We may consider entering other markets in the future when we have sufficient surplus capital to take measured exposure, but our immediate focus remains firmly on Dubai.
What is your outlook on the branded real estate market in the UAE, particularly Dubai, for the remainder of 2026 and 2027?

The branded residences market has already seen significant sales momentum and investor attention. We believe the next major phase will be project delivery, particularly from 2027 onwards. At that point, the market will increasingly move from evaluating branded residences based on sales momentum and marketing appeal to assessing their actual operational and investment performance.

We particularly see value in hospitality-branded residences, where experienced hospitality operators can bring stronger service standards, operational management and potentially higher rental performance. However, branding alone is not enough. Investors also need to consider the entry price and underlying economics of the investment.
Higher service charges may be justified where they translate into stronger rental performance and service levels, but ultimately the acquisition price remains critical to long-term returns.
